deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is German prose lecture or study notes on ancient Greek history, and it continues the narrative from folio 56 (the Dorian migration and the return of the Heracleidae, c. 1100–900 BC). Folio 58 goes on to the history of Sparta. The page covers the following:

(Heading) Greek national institutions: the festivals and games. These were held in honour of particular deities. The Olympic and Nemean games honoured Jupiter (Zeus), the Isthmian games honoured Neptune (Poseidon), and the Pythian games honoured Apollo. 'Neptuns' was written at the end of one line, struck out, and rewritten at the start of the next.

(1) Only Hellenes could take part, including those who had settled outside Greece. Women ('Damen') were excluded. The festivals served to promote national spirit and national union. Civic and physical skills were displayed, and learning and culture also benefited.

(2) The Amphictyonic Assembly at Delphi. It began as a league of the small peoples living around Delphi, who deliberated on matters concerning the cult of the Delphic Apollo. Later it grew: more Greek peoples joined and sent envoys, and it gradually became a kind of 'Reichstag' (diet) of all Greece.

No derivation, computation, or mathematical problem is present. The hand and content suggest school or lecture notes on ancient history bound into the bundle, rather than Gauss's mathematical work. Whether the hand is Gauss's own is uncertain.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics.

The history is standard textbook material of c. 1800 and broadly correct by period standards: the Olympian and Nemean games for Zeus, the Isthmian for Poseidon, the Pythian for Apollo, and the Delphic Amphictyony as a religious league that grew in importance.
Minor historical point: calling the Amphictyony a 'Reichstag of all Greece' is the conventional overstatement of older textbooks.
